# EvItem

> An item is a horizontal list row that pairs a leading element (icon, avatar, image) with a title and description, and an optional trailing action — used in lists, menus, and selection groups.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:item` |
| Layer | Molecule (`src/molecules`) |
| Import | `import { EvItem } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvItem>` or `<ev-item>` |
| Source | `src/molecules/item/EvItem.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-item">` |

## Example

```vue
<EvItem
  title="Alex Wijaya"
  description="alex@example.com"
/>
```

_The exact snippet the playground simulator copies for this component (`playground/simulator-demos.ts`)._

Its default slot is built to hold `EvLabelItem` (`evoq-ui:label-item`).

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Item**, frame `4282:80173` (Item). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use for rows in lists, menus, settings, or selection groups where each entry pairs a leading visual with a title, supporting text, and an optional action.

### When not to use

- Don't use for dense tabular data with many columns — use a Table. Don't use for a single standalone action — use a Button (`evoq-ui:button`).

### Do

- Keep one leading element per item and align trailing actions consistently down the list. Keep titles short and let the description carry detail.

### Don't

- Don't stack multiple leading visuals (avatar + image + icon) in one item. Don't crowd the row with several trailing actions — keep it to one.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvItem`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-item">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:item` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
